prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t name one single “best” roofer for all situations, but I can help you find a highly qualified Denver contractor and avoid scams. If you tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood I’ll pull together a short list of top-rated local roofers. Meanwhile, here’s a practical plan and checklist to get the right company for hail damage repair.

What to do now
- Get 2–3 written estimates from local roofing contractors experienced with hail claims.
- Notify your insurance company and document damage with photos before repairs start.
- Don’t sign anything or pay large upfront sums until you verify credentials and permits.

How to evaluate roofers
- Insurance/License: Verify the contractor carries general liability and workers’ comp insurance. (Ask for certificates.)
- Storm/insurance experience: Choose a contractor who routinely works with insurance adjusters and provides a line‑item estimate.
- Manufacturer certifications: Look for GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, Owens Corning Preferred, etc. These matter for warranty transfers.
- References and portfolio: Ask for recent local hail-repair references and photos.
- Written scope and warranty: Get a detailed, line-item proposal (materials, tear-off vs. overlay, flashing, vents) and written workmanship warranty.
- Permits: A reputable roofer pulls city/county permits for the work and arranges inspections.
- Materials: For hail-prone areas ask about impact-resistant (Class 4) shingles/options.

Where to check reputation
- Google Reviews, Yelp, Angi/HomeAdvisor, and the Better Business Bureau.
- Local Facebook groups or Nextdoor for neighborhood recommendations.
- Colorado license/registration checks if applicable and a web search for complaints or lawsuits.

Red flags / avoid
- Door‑to‑door "storm chasers" who pressure you to sign immediately.
- No local address or no insurance certificate.
- Asking for very large cash payments up front.
- Vague estimates (no line items, no materials specified).

If you want, give me your Denver ZIP code or neighborhood and I’ll list several well-reviewed roofing contractors nearby and note any online reputational issues for each.
